title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI
simple_definition: A system improves only when an external check confirms that its change is better.
visual_focus: Keep the agent, evaluator, verification gate, and skill library visible while a proposed change moves through them.

mapping.visual: a blue circle on the left
a score dial in the centre
a red or green gate after the evaluator
a stack of saved cards on the right

beats.narration: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI. A system improves only when an external check confirms that its change is better.
beats.visual: Show the title above four connected components: agent, evaluator, verification gate, and skill library.

beats.narration: An agent can call any change an improvement. Its own confidence does not prove the change works.
beats.visual: The agent sends a change directly toward the skill library. The verification gate turns red and blocks it.

beats.narration: The bounded loop sends each proposed change to an external evaluator.
beats.visual: A proposal dot moves from the agent to the evaluator along the existing arrow.

beats.narration: The evaluator scores the change against a fixed test. The verification gate opens only when that test passes.
beats.visual: The evaluator dial moves, then the gate changes from red to green.

beats.narration: The survey covers 1250 papers. It finds that 74% of deployment-time self-evolution papers were posted in 2026.
beats.visual: Keep the mechanism visible. Show 1250 above the evaluator and 74% beside the open gate.

beats.narration: The paper does not claim that frontier labs already run recursive self-improvement.
beats.visual: Draw a boundary after the skill library and dim everything beyond it.

beats.narration: Does your last self-improving pipeline climb the verification hierarchy, or does it just trust its own confidence?
beats.visual: Return focus to the evaluator and verification gate. Pulse the gate once while the question remains in the caption.
